newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's GPA Group year profits soar.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's GPA Group year profits soar.

text.p: Irish-based aircraft leasing firm GPA Group Plc said on Thursday its net profit soared to $105 million for the year ended on March 31 from $54 million the previous year.
GPA's annual revenue fell to $374 million from $1.14 billion, mainly due to the sale of 229 aircraft in March 1996, the company said.
GPA was taken over by U.S. group GE Capital Services after the collapse of GPA's flotation a number of years ago.
The company said it did not currently expect it would need to raise new debt or finance or sell assets to meet its existing obligations.
GPA's cash balance stood at $600 million at March 31 compared to $1.28 billion a year earlier, while borrowings were cut to $757 million from $1.58 billion.
Shareholders' funds rose to $277 million versus $166 million, the company said.
"The company's financial position is strong and positions GPA well to deal with future challenges and opportunities," chief executive Patrick Blaney said in the firm's earnings statement.
